proof:
Source: steps 9–11 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 6, 3.3–3.9; the integrality sketch 3.5–3.8 replaced by a bi-Lipschitz parametrization, tangent planes along the pieces and the area formula), generalized from the domain ℝ^P and K = spt Y to an open U and a compact K carrying Hⁿ⌞M. The parent's IMC(a) is the hypothesis (TL) here. As in the parent, the carrier is finally restricted to the points of nonzero multiplicity (oppositely oriented sheets with the same image cancel).
Notation and algebra. Hⁿ := μHE[n]; on ℝⁿ (Euclid n) it is Lebesgue measure Lⁿ. |α|_E := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I increasing} α(e_I)²)^{1/2} for a k-covector α (e the standard basis of ℝ^P). For a linear A : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P let A_#e be the n-vector α ↦ α(Ae₁, …, Aeₙ) (e₁, …, eₙ the standard basis of ℝⁿ) and J_A := det(⟨Ae_i, Ae_j⟩)^{1/2} ≥ 0 (the area Jacobian); for a linear L : ℝ^P → ℝ^P and an n-vector ζ let L_#ζ be the n-vector α ↦ ζ(α∘L), so (LA)_#e = L_#(A_#e). For g : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P differentiable at u, J_g(u) := J_{Dg(u)}. For orthonormal σ₁, …, σₙ, σ_# denotes the n-vector α ↦ α(σ₁, …, σₙ), a unit orientation of span σ. The following algebra (the parent's (L0)–(L2) and the polar/Gram–Schmidt remark of its step 10) is proved here.
(A0) For an n-covector β and an orthonormal family τ₁, …, τₙ: |β(τ)| ≤ |β|_E. Proof: for any orthonormal basis b of ℝ^P, S_b(β) := Σ_{i₁,…,iₙ} β(b_{i₁}, …, b_{iₙ})² does not depend on b (for fixed later arguments, Σ_i γ(b_i, w₂, …)² = |g|² with g the vector representing γ(·, w₂, …) — Parseval — and the slots can be changed one at a time), and S_e(β) = n!|β|²_E (tuples with a repeated index give 0; each injective tuple is a permutation of a unique increasing I and contributes β(e_I)²). Extending τ to an orthonormal basis b and keeping only the n! permutations of τ in S_b(β) gives n!β(τ)² ≤ n!|β|²_E.
(A1) Two unit orientations of the same n-plane differ by a sign: if τ, τ' are orthonormal bases of the plane then τ'_i = Σ_j O_{ij}τ_j with O := (⟨τ'_i, τ_j⟩) orthogonal, and multilinear alternating expansion gives α(τ') = det(O)·α(τ) with det O = ±1; so ±τ'_# = ±τ_#. Also −ζ is a unit orientation whenever ζ is.
(A2) Let A : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P be linear. If A is injective, let σ₁, …, σₙ be the Gram–Schmidt orthonormalization of Ae₁, …, Aeₙ, so Ae_j = Σ_{i≤j} T_{ij}σ_i with T upper triangular and T_{jj} = dist(Ae_j, span(Ae₁, …, Ae_{j−1})) > 0. Then (⟨Ae_i, Ae_j⟩) = TᵀT, so J_A = det T = Π_j T_{jj} > 0, and multilinear alternating expansion gives α(Ae₁, …, Aeₙ) = det(T)·α(σ) for every n-covector α, i.e. A_#e = J_A·σ_#, where σ_# is a unit orientation of span σ = A(ℝⁿ). In particular |A_#e(α)| ≤ J_A|α|_E by (A0). Moreover J_A ≤ Π_j|Ae_j| (Hadamard, since T_{jj} ≤ |Ae_j|). If A is not injective, (Ae_j) is linearly dependent, so A_#e = 0 (α alternating) and J_A = 0 (singular Gram matrix); the bounds hold trivially.
(A3) For linear A : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P and L : ℝ^P → ℝ^P: J_{LA} ≤ ‖L‖ⁿ·J_A. Proof: if A is not injective, neither is LA and both sides are 0. Otherwise, with σ and T from (A2) and V : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P the isometry Ve_i := σ_i (so A = VT), the Gram matrix of LAe is Tᵀ·(⟨Lσ_i, Lσ_j⟩)·T, hence J_{LA} = det(T)·J_{LV} = J_A·J_{LV}, and J_{LV} ≤ Π_i|Lσ_i| ≤ ‖L‖ⁿ by the Hadamard bound of (A2) applied to LV.
1. Reductions. (a) M₁ := M ∩ K is Borel, Hⁿ(M ∖ M₁) = 0 and Hⁿ(M₁) ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ (θ ≥ 1 on M; R.locallyIntegrable_mult). Hence Q(ω) = ∫_{M₁} θξ(ω(f(x))∘Df(x)) dHⁿ for all ω. (b) Oriented points: by (TL) with (U, A, B) := (U, M₁, M) (Hⁿ(M ∩ C) < ∞ for compact C ⊆ U), for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M₁ the sets M₁ and M have the same approximate tangent spaces at x; with R.orients, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M₁, M₁ has an approximate tangent space T_xM₁ at x (unique, SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique) and ξ(x) is a unit orientation of it. Fix a Borel ξ̃ equal to ξ Hⁿ-a.e. on M (a.e. strong measurability). (c) Cutoff: choose an open V ⊇ K with compact closure ⊆ O and χ ∈ C^∞(ℝ^P), 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1, tsupport χ ⊆ V, χ = 1 on an open W₀ ⊇ K; f̂ := χf on O, 0 off O, is C¹ on ℝ^P with compactly supported continuous derivative, hence Lipschitz on ℝ^P (mean value inequality), and f̂ = f on W₀; so f̂(x) = f(x), Df̂(x) = Df(x) for x ∈ K and Q is unchanged when f is replaced by f̂. From now on f denotes f̂; Λ := max(1, sup_K‖Df‖) < ∞.
2. Parametrization (parent step 9; the accepted DAG declaration dpf_rectifiable_bilipschitz_pieces states the measurable-piece version of (a)–(f), which a decomposition of this node may reuse before applying (g)). There are countably many triples (A_i, G_i, κ_i) with A_i ⊆ ℝⁿ compact, G_i : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P Lipschitz, differentiable at every u ∈ A_i with DG_i(u) injective, κ_i > 0 and |G_i(u) − G_i(v)| ≥ κ_i|u − v| for u, v ∈ A_i, such that the sets G_i(A_i) ⊆ M₁ are pairwise disjoint and Hⁿ(M₁ ∖ ⋃_i G_i(A_i)) = 0. Proof. (a) M₁ ⊆ M is countably n-rectifiable (CountablyRectifiable.mono): M₁ ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝⁿ) with Hⁿ(M₀) = 0 and F_j Lipschitz. (b) Rademacher (Mathlib LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt): D_j := {u : F_j differentiable at u} is Borel with Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ D_j) = 0, so Hⁿ(F_j(ℝⁿ ∖ D_j)) = 0 (Lipschitz images of null sets are null; Mathlib LipschitzWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le). (c) Z_j := {u ∈ D_j : DF_j(u) not injective} satisfies Hⁿ(F_j(Z_j)) = 0 (area formula, the Jacobian vanishing on Z_j; SimonGMT area_image_criticalSet_eq_zero). (d) E_j := (D_j ∖ Z_j) ∩ F_j⁻¹(M₁) is Borel. For injective linear A pick K_A > 0 with |Au| ≥ |u|/K_A and set r(A) := 1/(2K_A); r(A) := 1 otherwise. Mathlib exists_partition_approximatesLinearOn_of_hasFDerivWithinAt (F_j on E_j with derivative DF_j and this r) gives disjoint Borel t_l covering E_j and A_l = DF_j(y_l), y_l ∈ E_j (so A_l injective), with |F_j(u) − F_j(v) − A_l(u − v)| ≤ r(A_l)|u − v| on E_j ∩ t_l; hence |F_j(u) − F_j(v)| ≥ (2K_{A_l})⁻¹|u − v| there. (e) Enumerate the pieces E_j ∩ t_l as (E_i, G_i, κ_i) (G_i one of the F_j). Disjointify the images: E'_i := E_i ∖ G_i⁻¹(⋃_{i'<i} G_{i'}(E'_{i'})); each G_{i'}(E'_{i'}) is Borel by Lusin–Souslin (Mathlib MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn; G_{i'} continuous and injective on E_{i'}), so E'_i is Borel, and the G_i(E'_i) ⊆ M₁ are pairwise disjoint with the same union as the G_i(E_i). (f) M₁ ∖ ⋃_i G_i(E'_i) ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝⁿ ∖ D_j) ∪ ⋃_j F_j(Z_j) is Hⁿ-null. (g) G_i is injective on E'_i with (1/κ_i)-Lipschitz inverse, so Lⁿ(E'_i) ≤ κ_i^{−n}Hⁿ(M₁) < ∞; by inner regularity E'_i contains disjoint compact sets C_{i,1}, C_{i,2}, … with Lⁿ(E'_i ∖ ⋃_k C_{i,k}) = 0, whose complement's image under G_i is Hⁿ-null. Re-enumerate (C_{i,k}, G_i, κ_i) as (A_i, G_i, κ_i). ∎
3. Lemma T (parent step 10, specialized to globally Lipschitz maps, which covers every use below: the G_i of step 2 and H_i = f∘G_i of step 5). Let A ⊆ ℝⁿ be compact, G : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P Lipschitz on ℝⁿ, differentiable at every u ∈ A, and |G(u) − G(v)| ≥ κ|u − v| for u, v ∈ A (κ > 0). Then for Lⁿ-a.e. u ∈ A, V_u := DG(u)(ℝⁿ) is n-dimensional and HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (G(A)) (G(u)) V_u. Proof. (i) The set of differentiability points of G is Borel and u ↦ DG(u) is Borel on it (Mathlib measurableSet_of_differentiableAt, measurable_fderiv), with ‖DG(u)‖ ≤ Lip(G); so u ↦ 1_A(u)J_G(u) is bounded (by Lip(G)ⁿ, (A2)) and Borel. By the Lebesgue density and differentiation theorems (Mathlib ae_tendsto_average_norm_sub), Lⁿ-a.e. u ∈ A is a density point of A and a Lebesgue point of 1_A·J_G; fix such u. (ii) DG(u) is injective: for w ≠ 0, density gives points v_r ∈ A with |v_r − (u + rw)| = o(r) as r ↓ 0 (a ball of radius comparable to r about u + rw cannot miss A), and |DG(u)(v_r − u)| ≥ |G(v_r) − G(u)| − o(r) ≥ κ|v_r − u| − o(r), so |DG(u)w| ≥ κ|w|. Hence J_G(u) > 0 and dim V_u = n. (iii) Put x := G(u) and let h ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with tsupport h ⊆ B_ρ(0). By the scaling Hⁿ(η_{x,r}(S)) = r^{−n}Hⁿ(S) and the injective area formula for the Lipschitz map G on A, on which it is injective (SimonGMT weighted_area_formula_lipschitz_injOn, or injective_area_formula_lipschitzOn / weighted_area_formula_lipschitzOn_fiberSum; their Jacobian within A equals J_G at a.e. point of A), ∫_{η_{x,r}(G(A))} h dHⁿ = r^{−n}∫_A h((G(v) − x)/r)J_G(v) dv = ∫_{ℝⁿ} 1_A(u + rw)·h((G(u + rw) − G(u))/r)·J_G(u + rw) dw. The integrand vanishes unless |w| < ρ/κ (if u + rw ∈ A then |G(u + rw) − G(u)| ≥ κr|w|). On B_{ρ/κ}(0), (G(u + rw) − G(u))/r → DG(u)w uniformly as r ↓ 0 (differentiability at u), h is uniformly continuous and bounded, and ∫_{B_{ρ/κ}}|1_A(u + rw)J_G(u + rw) − J_G(u)| dw → 0 (u is a Lebesgue point of 1_A·J_G with value J_G(u)). So the integral tends to J_G(u)∫_{ℝⁿ} h(DG(u)w) dw = ∫_{V_u} h dHⁿ (area formula for the injective linear map DG(u)). As h is arbitrary, G(A) has approximate tangent space V_u at G(u). ∎
4. Tangent planes of M₁ and the orientation (★). Fix i. G_i(A_i) ⊆ M₁ is compact. By (TL) with (A, B) := (G_i(A_i), M₁), for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ G_i(A_i) the approximate tangent spaces of G_i(A_i) and M₁ at x agree. Since (G_i|A_i)⁻¹ is (1/κ_i)-Lipschitz, Hⁿ-null subsets of G_i(A_i) have Lⁿ-null preimages in A_i, and G_i maps Lⁿ-null sets to Hⁿ-null sets. With Lemma T and step 1(b): for Lⁿ-a.e. u ∈ A_i, x := G_i(u) is oriented, ξ̃(x) = ξ(x), and T_xM₁ = DG_i(u)(ℝⁿ). By (A2) with A := DG_i(u) (injective), DG_i(u)_#e/J_{G_i}(u) is a unit orientation of DG_i(u)(ℝⁿ) = T_xM₁, as is ξ(x); so by (A1), for such u,
 (★) ξ(G_i(u)) = s_i(u)·DG_i(u)_#e/J_{G_i}(u), s_i(u) ∈ {1, −1},
 where s_i(u) := 1 if ξ̃(G_i(u)) = DG_i(u)_#e/J_{G_i}(u) and −1 otherwise (Borel in u).
5. The maps H_i := f∘G_i (parent step 11). H_i is Lipschitz on ℝⁿ, differentiable at each u ∈ A_i with DH_i(u) = Df(G_i(u))∘DG_i(u) (chain rule), and DH_i(u)_#e = Df(G_i(u))_#(DG_i(u)_#e). By (★), for a.e. u ∈ A_i and every n-covector β: ξ(G_i(u))(β∘Df(G_i(u))) = s_i(u)·⟨β, DH_i(u)_#e⟩/J_{G_i}(u). By (A3), J_{H_i}(u) = J_{Df(G_i(u))DG_i(u)} ≤ ‖Df(G_i(u))‖ⁿJ_{G_i}(u) ≤ ΛⁿJ_{G_i}(u), and by (A2), |⟨β, DH_i(u)_#e⟩| ≤ J_{H_i}(u)|β|_E for every n-covector β (⟨β, ζ⟩ := ζ(β)).
6. Pulling Q back. The injective area formula for G_i on A_i (Hⁿ⌞G_i(A_i) is the image of J_{G_i}·Lⁿ⌞A_i under G_i) and step 2 give, with θ_i := θ∘G_i, for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U): Q(ω) = Σ_i ∫_{A_i} θ_i(u)s_i(u)⟨ω(H_i(u)), DH_i(u)_#e⟩ du, and Σ_i ∫_{A_i} θ_iJ_{H_i} du ≤ ΛⁿΣ_i∫_{A_i} θ_iJ_{G_i} du = Λⁿ∫_{M₁} θ dHⁿ < ∞, so the series converges absolutely (by step 5, the u-integrand is bounded by sup|ω|_E·θ_iJ_{H_i}).
7. Bi-Lipschitz pieces of H_i. Where DH_i(u) is not injective, DH_i(u)_#e = 0 (A2) and the integrand of step 6 vanishes. A_i⁺ := {u ∈ A_i : DH_i(u) injective} is Borel (u ↦ DH_i(u) is Borel on A_i; injectivity means det(⟨DH_i(u)e_p, DH_i(u)e_q⟩) ≠ 0). As in step 2(d), (g) (partition lemma with r(A) := 1/(2K_A), then inner regularity), A_i⁺ is, up to an Lⁿ-null set, a countable disjoint union of compact sets A_{il} with |H_i(u) − H_i(v)| ≥ κ_{il}|u − v| on A_{il}, κ_{il} > 0.
8. Image pieces. N_{il} := H_i(A_{il}) is compact and H_i|A_{il} is injective with (1/κ_{il})-Lipschitz inverse. Put g_{il} := (θ_is_i)∘(H_i|A_{il})⁻¹ on N_{il} (values in ℤ ∖ {0}) and η_{il} := (DH_i(·)_#e/J_{H_i}(·))∘(H_i|A_{il})⁻¹ (unit orientations of DH_i(u)(ℝⁿ) by (A2), Borel on N_{il}). The injective area formula for H_i on A_{il} turns step 6 into Q(ω) = Σ_{i,l} ∫_{N_{il}} g_{il}(y)⟨ω(y), η_{il}(y)⟩ dHⁿ(y), with Σ_{i,l}∫_{N_{il}} |g_{il}| dHⁿ = Σ_{i,l}∫_{A_{il}} θ_iJ_{H_i} du ≤ Λⁿ∫_{M₁}θ dHⁿ < ∞. N := ⋃_{i,l} N_{il} is Borel (σ-compact), N ⊆ f(M₁) ⊆ f(K) ⊆ U, and Hⁿ(N) ≤ Σ_{i,l}∫_{N_{il}}|g_{il}| < ∞ (|g_{il}| ≥ 1).
9. Common tangent planes. By Lemma T (H_i on A_{il}) and (TL) with (U, A, B) := (ℝ^P, N_{il}, N) (Borel, Hⁿ(N) < ∞), with the null-set transfer through the bi-Lipschitz map H_i|A_{il} as in step 4: for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ N and every (i, l) with y ∈ N_{il}, N has approximate tangent space T_yN = DH_i(u)(ℝⁿ), u := (H_i|A_{il})⁻¹(y) (countably many null exceptional sets). Hence η_{il}(y) is a unit orientation of T_yN, and by (A1) η_{il}(y) = ε_{il}(y)η(y) with ε_{il}(y) ∈ {±1}, where η(y) := η_{i₀l₀}(y) for the first piece (in a fixed enumeration) containing y; η is Borel. As Σ_{i,l}|g_{il}|1_{N_{il}} is integrable, Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ N lies in only finitely many N_{il}.
10. Integer multiplicity. For such y, Σ_{i,l} g_{il}(y)1_{N_{il}}(y)η_{il}(y) = k(y)η(y) with k(y) := Σ_{(i,l): y∈N_{il}} ε_{il}(y)g_{il}(y) ∈ ℤ (a finite sum) and |k| ≤ Σ_{i,l}|g_{il}|1_{N_{il}}. By dominated convergence (the partial sums are dominated by Σ|g_{il}|1_{N_{il}}·sup|ω|_E), Q(ω) = ∫_N k(y)⟨ω(y), η(y)⟩ dHⁿ(y) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U).
11. The representation (positive multiplicity). Choose a Borel Hⁿ-null N₀ ⊆ N off which steps 9–10 hold and k agrees with a Borel ℤ-valued k̃. Put N' := {y ∈ N ∖ N₀ : k̃(y) ≠ 0}, θ' := |k̃| (ℕ-valued, Borel) and ξ' := sign(k̃)·η. Then (N', θ', ξ') is an IMRep in U: N' is Borel and N' ⊆ N ⊆ U; N' is countably n-rectifiable (N ⊆ ⋃_i H_i(ℝⁿ) with H_i Lipschitz on ℝⁿ); θ' is measurable with θ' ≥ 1 on N'; ∫_{N'∩C} θ' dHⁿ ≤ Σ_{i,l}∫|g_{il}| < ∞ for every compact C; ξ' is Borel, hence a.e. strongly measurable; and by (TL) with (A, B) := (N', N), for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ N' the approximate tangent space of N' at y equals T_yN, which ξ'(y) = ±η(y) orients (IsUnitOrientationOf allows either sign). Finally, for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), ∫_{N'} θ'ξ'(ω) dHⁿ = ∫_{N'} k⟨ω, η⟩ dHⁿ = ∫_N k⟨ω, η⟩ dHⁿ = Q(ω), since k = 0 on N ∖ (N' ∪ N₀). So Q = τ(N', θ', ξ') and Q is integer multiplicity. ∎
key_steps: Restrict to M₁ = M ∩ K (Hⁿ(M₁) < ∞), use (TL) for oriented points, and cut f off to a globally Lipschitz C¹ map agreeing with f near K.
Parametrize M₁ up to a null set by disjoint compact bi-Lipschitz pieces G_i(A_i) (Rademacher, critical-set area formula, partition lemma, Lusin–Souslin, inner regularity).

Lemma T (globally Lipschitz G, bi-Lipschitz on compact A): at density/Lebesgue points the blow-ups of G(A) converge to the plane DG(u)(ℝⁿ); with (TL) and the Gram–Schmidt algebra (A0)–(A3), T_{G_i(u)}M₁ = DG_i(u)(ℝⁿ) and ξ(G_i(u)) = s_i(u)·DG_i(u)_#e/J_{G_i}(u).
With H_i = f∘G_i and the area formula, Q(ω) = Σ_{i,l}∫_{N_{il}} g_{il}⟨ω, η_{il}⟩ dHⁿ over compact bi-Lipschitz image pieces N_{il} = H_i(A_{il}), with Σ∫|g_{il}| ≤ Λⁿ∫_{M₁}θ.
Lemma T and (TL) make every η_{il}(y) = ±η(y) for one orientation η of T_yN, so Q(ω) = ∫_N k⟨ω, η⟩ with k integer-valued; (N′, |k|, sign(k)η) on {k ≠ 0} is an IMRep representing Q.
